LESSON: READING 7.4.1 CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers, part of Strand 7 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story? 2. How would you describe the behaviour of your classmates?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read and identify minor characters in a class reader,

2. search online and offline for words and phrases used to describe relationships between characters,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read and identify minor characters in a class reader,
2. search online and offline for words and phrases used to describe relationships between characters,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking: It is developed as the learner links the relationships between characters in the class reader.

• Collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner observes the rules of engagement while engaging in hot seating different minor

characters in the class reader to bring out their relationships.

Values:
Social justice is developed as the learner discusses the relationships between characters in a class reader.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Citizenship is enhanced as the learner discusses the character traits and relationships of the characters in the class reader.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of relationship of characters in a class reader to their learning of characterisation in Creative Arts.
